paper_title: 1+12 Can Large Language Models Serve as Cross-Lingual Knowledge   Aggregators
caption: Statistics of the dataset in our experiments.
model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of data across five distinct categories used in the experiments described in the paper “1+12 Can Large Language Models Serve as Cross-Lingual Knowledge Aggregators.” The largest segment, colored red, represents TriviaQA, comprising 46% of the dataset (1,829 instances). The second largest, in purple, is WebQA at 25% (997 instances). Green represents HalluEval with 18% (721 instances), followed by a yellow segment for the Chinese Domain at 6% (231 instances), and a small light blue slice for HalluQA at 5% (185 instances). Each slice is labeled with its category name, percentage, and absolute count, and the chart uses a 3D effect with a slight separation of the TriviaQA slice to emphasize its dominance. No legend is present, as labels are directly attached to each segment. The proportions visually reflect the relative scale of each component in the experimental dataset.
